spans.s:
Nair-ukta in the nirukta denotes a man who knows the true etymology of words, and explains their meaning accordingly. Yāska's nirukta is the classic work of this school, and forms a commentary on an earlier nirukta, the so-called Naighaṇṭuka, a glossary consisting of five collections of Vedic words.
Foot notes ‘One concerned with etymological explanation’ (nir-ukta).
i. 12; vi. 11; xi. 19. 29. 31; xii. 10; xiii. 9.
Cf. Weber, Indian Literature, 26, 85; Indische Studien, 2, 39, n.; Sieg, Die Sagenstoffc des ṛgveda, 10-13; Muir, Sanskrit Texts, 2^2, 165 et seq.
